title: China Is Raising the Stakes in Latin America
gist: Margaret Myers argues China's Latin America strategy is narrowing to export-linked, tech-driven priorities under its 15th Five-Year Plan, with a $46 billion regional trade deficit in 2025 and a flood of cheap Chinese goods, while Latin American states are squeezed between Washington and Beijing.

insights.claim: China-Latin America trade rose 3% between 2024 and 2025 and the core drivers, commodity acquisition and exporting to regional markets, remain intact despite Trump's 'Donroe Doctrine'.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Structural trade ties persist despite US pressure.

insights.claim: China has swapped large loans and mega-projects for smaller deals supporting its own industrial and export interests; in 2023 about 60% of Chinese FDI in the region went to 'New Infrastructure' sectors such as telecommunications, fintech and energy.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Chinese capital is concentrating in tech-driven sectors, not roads and ports.
insights.locator: I also noted that China had reworked

insights.claim: China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) prioritizes export growth and support for national champions, and with less overseas lending capacity Beijing is being more selective.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Expect fewer big Chinese financings and more export push.
insights.locator: These trends appear to be deepening

insights.claim: Chinese greenfield investment in the region spiked almost 400% last year only because of one $39 billion ByteDance-backed data center in Brazil; excluding it the trend is downward and concentrated, with about 30% going to advanced manufacturing and ICT.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Headline Chinese FDI growth is a one-project outlier.
insights.locator: This is reflected in China's greenfield investment

insights.claim: Latin American imports from China have outpaced exports to China since 2021, producing a $46 billion trade deficit in 2025 per Chinese Customs data.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Rising deficit is fuelling protectionist responses.
insights.locator: As Beijing works to offload excess industrial capacity

insights.claim: The region should expect more Chinese exports, from EVs and industrial machinery to large volumes of low-cost e-commerce goods, as Chinese firms in brutal domestic price wars seek buyers even in the smallest markets.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Price deflation pressure on local manufacturers, autos and retail.

insights.claim: Mexico has nearly doubled its anti-dumping filings against Chinese goods and floated tariffs on over a thousand Chinese product lines including autos, textiles and steel, while Brazil has deepened ties with Beijing on soy, beef and energy and Chile has split the difference.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Divergent national alignments create country-specific trade risks.
insights.locator: Latin American countries are taking different paths

insights.claim: China is acting more assertively to protect assets and market access, launching counter-investigations and warning governments against capitulation to Washington, while US posture has shifted from scrutiny of specific security risks to near-blanket suspicion of anything China-led.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Both sides escalating raises the cost of fence-sitting for regional governments.
insights.locator: All of these paths carry costs

insights.claim: The Trump administration is unlikely to change course because there is an apparent consensus in Washington that economic and military coercion is achieving desired effects in the region.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: Expect continued US pressure on the region.
insights.quote: economic and military coercion is achieving desired effects in the region

insights.claim: Regional enthusiasm for closer ties to China has cooled because of unresolved debt obligations, unmaterialized diplomatic payoffs or underwhelming returns from Chinese manufacturing investment.
insights.speaker: MARGARET MYERS
insights.so_what: China's soft power in the region is weaker than headline trade suggests.
